text: Course 8 of this catalog built out real Change Enablement on ServiceNow: Normal, Standard, and Emergency change types, CAB review, approvals, and a full record of who authorized what, and when. That whole apparatus assumes a Change Request is explicitly created, by a person or a well-defined process.

Modern teams often build and deploy code through an external CI/CD pipeline — a tool like Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or Azure DevOps — with no ServiceNow instance involved at all. Left alone, that pipeline has no reason to know Change Management exists. Code can move from a commit to a production deployment entirely outside the governed process Course 8 spent a whole course building, not because anyone decided to skip it, but because nothing told the pipeline to check in.

ServiceNow DevOps is a dedicated application built specifically to close that gap. It isn't a CI/CD engine itself — it doesn't build code or run deployments. It sits alongside the platform's existing Change Enablement capabilities and gives external pipelines a structured way to talk to ServiceNow: registering pipeline tools and tracking the orchestration steps of a software delivery process.

The single most important capability, for this course's purposes, is this: ServiceNow DevOps can automatically create and update Change Request records that correspond to real pipeline events. When a pipeline run reaches a deployment stage, the app can generate the matching Change Request, with real details about what's deploying and through which pipeline run. A deployment through an external pipeline doesn't have to be invisible to Change Management just because a human didn't manually open a request for it — the pipeline event becomes the trigger, and the resulting Change Request is subject to the same rules Course 8 taught, not a shortcut around them.

That's the foundation the rest of this chapter builds on. Lesson 19 then covers the real tension this creates between moving fast and keeping control. Next up, though: how ServiceNow DevOps actually connects to an external pipeline tool, through real APIs and webhooks.
